items.name: ACID transactions
items.explanation: A transaction groups several changes so they all happen or none do. ACID names the guarantees: atomic, consistent, isolated and durable. On one database the engine enforces them; across shards it no longer can.

assumedBy.quote: When a table is split across multiple physical databases, we lose many of the reliability and consistency properties that we take for granted in ACID SQL databases.

sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: InnoDB and the ACID Model

items.name: Transaction ID wraparound
items.explanation: Postgres numbers transactions with a counter that eventually wraps. Vacuum has to keep marking old rows so the counter can be reused safely, and if vacuum falls behind, the database is in danger.

assumedBy.quote: While disk capacity can be increased, more worrying was the prospect of transaction ID (TXID) wraparound, a safety mechanism in which Postgres would stop processing all writes to avoid clobbering existing data.

sources.title: PostgreSQL docs: Routine Vacuuming (preventing transaction ID wraparound failures)

items.name: SQL views
items.explanation: A view is a saved query that you read like a table. The query runs each time the view is used, so a view can show part of a table without copying it.

assumedBy.quote: By creating sharded views on top of our existing unsharded physical databases, we could logically shard before we performed any risky physical reshard operations.

items.name: Foreign keys and unique indexes
items.explanation: A foreign key makes the database refuse a row that points at a missing row in another table. A unique index refuses duplicates. Both only work when the database can see all the rows, which sharding breaks.

assumedBy.quote: Foreign keys and globally unique indexes can no longer be enforced by Postgres.

sources.title: PostgreSQL docs: Constraints (unique constraints and foreign keys)

items.name: Query parsing and planning
items.explanation: A database parses SQL into a tree, then plans how to run it. Figma's proxy repeats those steps to decide which shards a query touches.

assumedBy.quote: A query parser reads SQL sent by the application and transforms it into an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).
